I will do it the way I have seen work around Quzhou for years, with a few careful adjustments. My land is only 1.2 mu, so every bag of fertilizer costs real money, but I still do not want to be short on fertilizer and lose yield. For winter wheat, I will stay with improved seed, put enough base fertilizer before sowing, and then topdress once when it greens up and once around jointing if the crop looks strong enough. Wheat here responds well to water, so with my well I will give it about 3 irrigations in a normal year. For summer maize after wheat, I will use hybrid seed because that is what gives steady ears in my area. I will keep fertilizer a bit heavier on maize than wheat, because maize eats fertilizer fast in summer and I would rather spend a bit more than watch the leaves go pale. I will do rotary tillage because my plot is small and that is the easiest way to handle the wheat-maize rotation. On pests, I will not spray too many times, just enough to keep aphids, armyworm, and common leaf disease under control if they show up. I start from what I did before, then look at moisture, seedling stand, and what nearby farmers are doing, and I adjust a little but not too much because big changes are risky on a small plot.
